maker: Honda Motor Co. (American Honda Motor Co., Inc.)
name: Honda Autonomous Work Vehicle, 3rd generation
summary: All-electric off-road flatbed robot vehicle from Honda that drives pre-set routes on large construction sites on its own (GPS, lidar, radar) or by remote control, carrying two pallets or up to 2,000 lb. An earlier generation hauled materials, water and supplies on a Black & Veatch solar construction site.

germany.statusNote: Prototype in the USA. Honda said in March 2023 it aims to commercialise the AWV and was looking for field-test, distribution and support partners; no sale, price or European route found.

specs.label: Max. loading capacity
specs.quote: Increased bed size to 2 pallets and greater loading capacity of 2000 pounds

specs.label: Max. speed, autonomous
specs.conditions: 2.5 mph by default under remote control

specs.label: Range at max. load
specs.quote: Up to 28 miles depending on the use case

specs.label: Operating time
specs.quote: Increased battery size and longer operating time of up to 10 hours

specs.label: Sensors
specs.value: GPS/GNSS, radar and lidar for obstacles, cameras for remote monitoring; lidar navigation where GNSS is weak
specs.quote: using GPS for location, radar and lidar for obstacle detection and cameras for remote monitoring

notes: Built on Honda's off-road side-by-side platform and described as a rugged off-road work vehicle; rough ground is the maker's claim.
Routes and stop points are set on a tablet; several vehicles can work together.
carryPayloadKg converts the stated 2,000 lb; the second generation carried nearly 900 lb and towed over 1,600 lb in the field test.
Honda says the specifications may still change as development continues.

images.credit: Honda Motor Co. (American Honda Motor Co., Inc.)

evidence.task: Several AWVs towed trailers and carried construction materials, water and supplies to pre-set points across a 1,000-acre solar construction site for a month
evidence.where: Black & Veatch solar construction site, New Mexico, USA
evidence.note: Second-generation prototype, the predecessor of this vehicle; operated by trained Black & Veatch staff for up to eight hours in high heat.

openQuestions: Is the AWV still in development or offered commercially after 2023? No newer source was read.
